summary: This paper investigates the evolution of minimum root spacing and ratios under finite free additive and multiplicative convolutions. The author discovers a sharp structural phase transition at d = 3 -> 4: while d <= 2, 3 obey exact Euclidean and hyperbolic Pythagorean laws, Pythagorean superadditivity universally fails for all d >= 4 due to Sturm-Liouville oscillations of Hermite heat flow. Furthermore, the macroscopic limit connects to Voiculescu's R-transform and the Basel constant pi^2/12. All algebraic cores and bounding inequalities are fully verified in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry.
strengths: Discovery of the sharp degree-3-to-4 phase transition in finite free root-gap dynamics.
Exact Euclidean and hyperbolic Pythagorean laws for degrees 2 and 3 with complete equality characterizations.
Complete formal verification of 16 core theorems in Lean 4 with zero axioms and zero sorry.
Bridges finite free convolution heat-flow dynamics with classical Sturm-Liouville oscillation theory and macroscopic R-transforms leading to the Basel constant.
weaknesses: The exact global infimum for the Pythagorean constant cd when d >= 4 remains open beyond bounds and degree-4 self-convolution counterexamples.
Asymptotic behavior of high-degree extremal gap configurations relies on heuristic and numerical convergence conjectures.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal Finite Free Marcel Riesz Monotonicity yielding 1/2-Pythagorean floors for all d >= 2.
Exact hyperbolic Pythagorean identity for degree-2 multiplicative convolution and cubic mu-supermultiplicativity for degree-3.
Sharp finite free heat-flow gap expansion theorem and universal d >= 4 failure via Sturm-Liouville comparison.
Voiculescu R-transform analytic continuation yielding the exact Basel limit pi^2/12 for free additive self-convolutions.
